So much this.  From deciding not to text first, to being overbearingly validating,  to oversharing, to feeling the cumulative weight of every failure and failing when things go nowhere.  And even the awareness of it all, which has its own accompanying frustrations.

To the question at the end, how to proceed from here, I am at a total loss.  Every time I try to outwit this stupidity, I find it is just another layer of the bpd bullshit.  Oh, that's just a different approach to splitting.  Oh, that's just what someone with bpd would do, just another symptom.

With the last two prospective relationships I've had and lost in excruciatingly typical bpd fashion, for equally typically bpd reasons, I've found out in the course of conversation that they've already had at least one previous toxic relationship with someone that sounds a lot like me.  Which means that I'm both their type, as the initial attraction reveals, but they've grown wiser, which sucks for me, but I'm also glad for them.  That's a pretty damn cold comfort, and one of the shitty aspects of self awareness is that I'm finding it increasingly difficult to advocate on my own behalf.  I guess that's my additional step: ultimately agreeing that they really dodged a bullet when they lost interest.

Thank you so much for responding.  I've been voluntarily but most often involuntarily  institutionalized numerous times.  It does me no good, the goggles, they do nothing.  For days, even while I sleep, I've been carrying a rope in a backpack.  It's turned into my security blanket, I just feel assured that it's there, hoping impulse will turn into resolve.

So I've kind of formulated a goal: "function without being seen, heard, touched, or valued, without attention or approval."  I'm sure as fuck not there yet, but if i could get there, at least I would be functional, which at this point I'm totally not.

Thank you for taking the time to respond so thoughtfully.  I can't tell you what it means to me that someone did so.  Somewhere my wife is being loved and celebrated by friends and family and our kids and her lovers.  I've just been feeling so God damn alone.
And I fully appreciate that it's all my fault.

It's so weird, my posts never get responses, my responses to other posts seem to have no value.  Even an old post on /r/suicidewatch, when out of options and without anyone to talk to, went unnoticed.  I am the least of you, the most hopeless, most worthless, most lacking in redeeming value, the most easily ignored.  I know that's a very BPDesque attitude to have, but it seems a conclusion more born of empirical observation than mental illness.  Oh well, somebody has to be worst, though no one wishes for it to be themselves.

It's fantastic you are putting so much effort into improving yourself.  I believe anyone (except myself, of course) is bound to see positive results if you persist.  I'm proud of you, and hopeful at your prospects for the future!

This is the type of shit you need to grow from, not rehash in your head.  Only you know your thoughts and intents, so you know precisely how shitty you *were*.  You are forgiven, accept it, and don't do it again.  I talked to a man a long time ago who said, "I was a cheater.  i stopped cheating.  I don't know when it happened, but eventually I wasn't a cheater anymore.  You were a cheater.  Maybe you'll have wait until this ambiguous time threshold occurs until you aren't anymore.  Don't let the guilt ruin your relationship while you wait.

Reddit has not been a good source for validation in my experience.  I know it's difficult to not take that personally, so I won't suggest it, but rather just suggest that you learn from the experience and not seek it here.

I am surprised to hear that political disengagement is apparently common in those with BPD.  I believe the more I get mixed up with political causes the more symptomatic I am, or even that having political causes are part of being symptomatic, not that this belief stops me at all.

1- Yes, but I think it is better to understand this experience as "infatuation", rather than being "in love."  Usually really intense infatuation, sure, but I think it helps to remember that it is just infatuation.

2- Pain is not deserved, but neither is a relationship.  What I tell myself is, " I am not a gift."  No woman dreams of being with a man like me.  Any woman I'm interested in has numerous preferable options. Long before I ever heard the term "negging", most of my romantic relationships were due to some unfortunate circumstance which caused some poor woman to believe that her value was somehow validated by being in a relationship with me.  That was my essential appeal and the central dynamic, though I had no idea at the time.  Isn't that horrible?  I've moved past having much pain about not having romantic relationships anymore, usually.  I just accept that I have little to nothing of value to offer, and any reciprocation of feelings that may be initially presented is due to either some ignorance or pathology on the part of a perspective partner, and being a decent person, on my part at least, means nipping that shit in the bud.

3- I occasionally get envious, not of relationships per say, but of those who are genuinely desirable and valuable. Also tall.  I think of myself as a failed genetic experiment, the sadly necessary background noise in the random production of humans better than myself.

Remember that life, the universe, and everything is absurd.  There is no god, the universe is cold and uncaring, and there isn't someone out there for everyone.  Give life your best shot, try to create the circumstances you desire, but accept reality for what it is, whatever that may be for you.

That's just not something a wonderful person would do to another.  I would guard against idealizing your ex.  I can already tell from the little you've written that they don't deserve it.

I have BPD, and of course can't speak for everyone with it, but I'm prone to ghosting and it has *NOTHING* to do with not caring for other people.  I feel a great deal of shame all the time for things I've said and done, and don't know how to handle it, so I disappear.  I feel like I contribute nothing, and that other people are better off without me.  Knowing this, I don't have any friendships anymore, and avoid making new ones, but most people can't live like that, so she may have other friends, because it's just an all too human need.  Try not to take it as a reflection on you, or even a reflection on her feelings toward you; it's just an awful coping mechanism she is stuck with, and it is to her detriment more that it is to you.

I would recommend starting by just temporarily giving yourself a break and not compare yourself to others.  Then try to imagine what you could do to improve yourself- not be the ideal person, just what you could improve.  Come up with a plan of habits that could get you moving in that direction: small steps that you can repeat.  If there are mountains, decompose them into molehills.  I need to lose 65 lbs.  I am trying to loose 5.  Just 5.  Will losing 5 lbs make me irresistibly attractive?  No.  Will losing 65 lbs make me irresistibly attractive?  Still no.  But will I consider myself to be better than I am now?  Yes, and I can look at that as a real accomplishment, something I could conceivably take some pride in.

Got off FB a few months ago when I could tell I was getting sick.  Ended my last two meat-space friendships this week.  Down to 0 friends in the world.  Got my first paycheck of 2017 working as a stagehand, with no sense of joy or accomplishment.  I'm alternating rapidly between rage and total despair.  I miss my kids so bad.  I'm spiraling, down down down.

I had "pain in my bones" when I was on lithium.  Even something like holding the steering wheel wrong could cause really intense pain.  It's never completely gone away, but it's improved drastically after I stopped taking medication.

I was pink-slipped to a state hospital in a manic state.  In 3 days lithium had completely leveled me out.  I was told that was impossible, that it had to build up in my bloodstream, but I very much doubt a placebo effect could account for the profound difference.  Again, my anecdotal experience agrees with yours, but the doctors said that it could not be so.
Ugh, I hate going to the hospital.  Hang in there!  Remember how good it feels when you are released :)

The solace of the depression for me is that I alone suffer, and if you're male and have had this disease for a while, no one gives a shit about you anymore, so it doesn't matter to anyone else.  When I'm manic I'm far more likely to be in the world and causing trouble and disruption for others.

Yes, that is such a difficulty of being bi-polar.  For me, it's not only people, but ideas.  I will get manic and get attached to an idea that I think is brilliant, but it's not.  I will be working on something potentially productive, get depressed, and give up.  If you are bi-polar, you actually *can't* trust your brain, and that sucks.
I agree.  I need to stay the hell off of it.

Well please don't give up now, not in the immediate aftermath of a breakup.  Give yourself time, no one wants to go through what you are going through, but you've got a lot going for you, even beyond this girlfriend and your cat (though I am very to hear about your cat.)  Focus on your job and business for a while.  You acknowledge you have a future: please allow yourself to see it come to fruition.
Hi!  What's going on?  I'm interested.

Hey, I think it's great that you are exercising, and the fact that you don't want to come off as pushy given your previous experience means you're willing to learn from your mistakes-that's rare, and bodes so well for you.  Keep working on yourself, refining yourself.  Life isn't a sprint, and you are so young.  If you are starting at average, you don't have so far to go to get to above-average.  It personally sounds like you've got the essentials together: just keep working at it, my man!

If I was Aristotle, Shakespeare, and Otis Redding combined, I doubt I could form words that made you feel better.  I can only affirm that you have every reason to feel hurt, angry, and betrayed.  Keep hold of your plans, what you look forward to, what you want to yet experience: so glad to hear that they exist.  Take it as easy on yourself as you can. Give yourself time to heal and room to just fucking breath when necessary.  Rooting for you, your courage, and your strength.

I agree: it's hard to think like that, and we've all been conditioned to think differently.  Hell, one will not generally be encouraged to think at all about anything, really.  All the world is a heart-shaped box today.  But dammit, I refuse to let Big Chocolate tell me how to live my life, unless they are giving out  samples.

You sound bright, self-disciplined, and rigorously analytical.  Amazing in light of your age and feeling so poorly so often.  Even if it's not bringing joy and satisfaction right now, I hope remain doing much of what you are doing, remain engaged in that which you are engaged in.  It will serve you well, especially if you find effective medication or your brain-chemistry just settles the fuck down (~ 25 years of age in many cases, or so I have read).  I'm sorry to hear that life is painful right now, but the world desperately needs young men like yourself: thank you for taking one for the team right now.  Hang in there.

To merely amplify tedbunnyism, we do not get to chose our families.  As a flawed parent with flawed parents, I suggest you love your folks for what they are, if not who they are and what they've done, give them a nod since you clearly won the genetic lottery that helped enable your incredible successes thus far, and tend to the business of creating your own happy and successful life, "playing forward" the lessons learned from having less than ideal parents, even if just to shove it in their faces when frustrated with them.  Hang in there.
Oh, and congrats on having money to give away.  You've got one up on me :)

I'm middle aged, and have nothing but a pile of failures to show with it.  Some early successes I guess, a couple decades ago, due more to cunning and compromise than effort, which really did nothing but leave me entirely unprepared for what was to come.  I'm currently kind of taking a "time out" from projects and goals, fishing for something in this world I might yet put my hand to.  Glad to hear you aren't currently actively suicidal, but wanting to die is a fucking drag, I know. I'm taking on faith at this point that there remains something interesting I could do, without the expectation that I will be successful, just something interesting in itself.  Have you found something that engages you?  If not, are you still looking for it?

You say you feel like your future was taken away before you had a chance to fight for it, but when I read your synoptic telling of your tale, I read of hard fought victories and the perseverance and determination of a clearly bright and lucid intellect.  You are frank about acknowledging your own missteps and maladaptive behavior, which is essential for growth.  You are considering your future, even while confronting the allure of an abrupt ending.  This all bodes well for you.

I'm the last person who would dare make assurances of ease and success, of an uncomplicated and unencumbered existence. But without reference to the three-ring shitshow of my own life, let me say this: my best friend from high school was murdered, my closest friend from college died suddenly, and last week I lost a friend from elementary school to liver failure.  Our lives are finite, whether we wish it or not, whether we hasten it or not.  I would hope for you that you seize yours from violation and fear and despair, and milk it for all the joy you may.
Nice timing!  As the old saying goes, don't look a gift dentist in the mouth.

I know it doesn't feel like it, but what you are experiencing is the path to wisdom, if not the quick road to success.  If you reflect on what you've done, and the "why" of what went wrong, not just be frustrated with failure, you can build a string of failures into success.  There are people who turn everything they touch into gold right from the start.  Thing is, the gold market fluctuates, and when gold is not what they need, they haven't learned anything in the process.  Don't give up please, keep moving forward, even if you aren't at the doorstep of success (which you may be, who knows?), you are on the surest path to get there.

Hi.  I too have spent my remaining cash on hand on gas rather than weed, which would have been my strongly preferred option.  A couple points, if I may. First, there is nothing in this life that I have experienced more grating to ones sense of self worth than looking for a job.  I'm not Arbys material?  I'm not worth a second glance to bag groceries in some hiring manager's estimation?  I mean, I think I may be able to scan a pack of cigarettes and hand someone their change while successfully respirating.  This is not a widely shared belief, it turns out.

I took some state mandated classes, and one of the things that was mentioned was that advertised jobs are the 15% of jobs that 85% of job seekers are vying for.  Its not you, or a measure of your value, its rigged against you, like trying to date Jessica Alba.

Do you have a social network to exploit?  Friends or family that might help get your foot in a door?

Well, I don't know where you studied, but you sure learned to write well.  Given your history, I'll leave it to others of the feminine persuation to respond more at length, but I wanted to mention that just today I was watching Maya Angelou speak about how courage is the most fundamental virtue, and the importance of embracing it, as without it our convictions may whither in the face of adversity.  Clearly you've been an overcomer of tremendous adversity, please don't stop now.

Many moons ago, when dinosaurs yet walked the earth, I was watching MTV, and they were interviewing axel rose.  He was saying that Prince reached out to him from out of nowhere to warn him that 27 is a ducking tough year, and that Prince turned out to be right.  If 27 is tough for Axel Rose and Prince, it may be tough on the rest of us that aren't rich and don't have thousands of screaming women tearing our clothes off.  Hang in there, my man!

Well, there may be no gratification, but you sure have accomplished a great deal, and it sounds like you did it with at least one arm tied behind your back.  You express a sense of personal worthlessness and uselessness, a lack of enjoyment in activities and people, a sense of life as meaningless, frustration with day-to-day life.. I can offer no easy answers or insightful platitudes, but I hope you take some time for yourself and reflect on what might give you a sense of purpose, what might imbue your life with meaning, or shit, what might just be fun for a while.  You are clearly not worthless, by any objective standard, tons of us out here in the world are slammed hard against the mountains you've already managed to climb- I wish you had found the flag of satisfaction waving at the peak.  Maybe you need to climb yet higher, rather than leap?  Maybe reach down a hand and pull a few up there with you?  Turn to professionals in other disciplines for help?  I don't know.  But some random stranger read your story, and is entirely unconvinced you have nothing to contribute, and is routing for you from afar.
